newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Mobile phone sales depend on renewals - Ericsson.
newsitem.headline: Mobile phone sales depend on renewals - Ericsson.

text.p: Swedish telecoms group Ericsson said on Friday that mobile phone market growth will depend more on how often customers buy new phones than on new customers getting subscriptions.

"We believe in sales of between 200 million and 300 million phones in the year 2000 and only 100 million of those are expected to be sold to new subscribers, assuming our forecasts are right," Jan Ahrenbring, marketing manager at Ericsson Mobile Communications, told Reuters.

Ericsson forecasts there will be about 500 million subscribers worldwide at the turn of the century. It will therefore make a big difference if every third or every fourth subscriber throws out an old phone to buy a new, Ahrenbring said.
"We are trying to work with different models when it comes to estimating this and some factors play a part, among them the number of operators," Ahrenbring said.
He saw Sweden was a leading country in terms of competition among operators.
At the end of 1995, Sweden had about 1.7 million mobile phone subscribers.
In 1996 another 500,000 subscribers were added but at the same time one million new phones were sold, showing that 30 percent of existing subscribers bought a new phone.

Internationally, only 15 million of 65 million sold phones were renewals, meaning that every sixth existing subscriber bought a new phone. At the end of 1995, the number of worldwide subscribers totalled 90 million.
"Understanding the 'renewal market' is an important part of trying to understand the future," Ahrenbring said.
He expected Ericsson to be well positioned as it has ranked well in customer satisfaction surveys.
"We know that we have more loyalty than other brands on several markets," Ahrenbring said.
